common_mistakes.mistake: A single hero waits on RESTORE or one stands on the other rather than both touching the pad.
common_mistakes.consequence: Weight remains below2, lift stays unpowered; neither weight1 nor height stacking is a substitute for two pad contacts.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reposition both side by side on the attached pad; the low deck is safe and no fast simultaneous key press is required.

confidence_reason: Current source, retained idle PNGs and accepted ordinary-input browser endpoint establish mechanics and one feasible route. Difficulty is an expert estimate; human discovery, errors, recovery behavior, enjoyment and physical keyboard comfort remain unmeasured.

confirmed: Joint restoration, controlled boarding/upper transfer and repeatable safe missed-lift recovery are confirmed; six known dimension scores and clarity remain the same.
missed_mechanics: RESTORE is physically attached to the carrier; both separate bodies must touch its weight2 pad. It powers permanently and also opens DNA. Pac can board first and wait; simultaneous takeoff is unnecessary.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass left Isp following the DNA opener unresolved; source establishes that the wall blocks Pac, so Isp requires no reopened passage. The first-pass risk of stranding Isp is not a real barrier failure mode.
changed_judgments: recovery_cost null -> 1: lower-floor geometry, persistent power latch and current accepted joint-board route support local missed-ride retries, replacing the first-pass unknown.
All other dimension scores are retained: joint weight changes the causal explanation without requiring narrow synchronized input; safe floor keeps hazard0. Control friction stays null.
unresolved: No human novice/paired-keyboard observation; prior exposure offers learning rather than proving mastery.
Common-mistake recovery descriptions are source-derived possibilities, not witnessed player errors.

No alternative ordinary-input route bypassing joint RESTORE is verified; apparent generic sequential-ride helper code is unreachable in the accepted branch. Exotic interference shortcuts are not assumed.

single_operator_note: One operator must hold Isp while moving Pac through DNA, then bring both into separate RESTORE contact and manage two sets of boarding/transfer keys. Pac can wait on the low carrier, reducing simultaneous key demand; this extra management is outside two-human scores.
